sam: heads up, ran into a flake with the py-sdk async client + OTEL middleware + structlog. request_id sometimes gets reused across concurrent requests when using the shared AsyncClient.
maria: can you paste a tiny repro?
sam: super small - two tasks set a contextvar and call the sdk client concurrently. intermittently both logs show the same id.
sam: ```python
import asyncio
import contextvars
from redwood.sdk import AsyncClient

request_id = contextvars.ContextVar('request_id', default=None)

async def do(i):
    request_id.set(f"r-{i}")
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        await c.get('https://internal/service')

asyncio.run(asyncio.gather(do(1), do(2)))
```
sam: repro ~1/30 runs locally.
derek: that looks like a shared mutable headers map in our async middleware path. in sync path we copy per-request, but optimized async path reused a dict. bad idea.
jean: also our middleware hooks are untyped so it's easy for middleware authors to mutate state. we should define a TypedRequest/Headers Protocol in the public types.
maria: we also have background tasks the SDK spawns for streaming cleanup. if those tasks don't capture contextvars at schedule time, they can also cause cross-request leakage. worth auditing create_task usage.
derek: short-term fix: make middleware build a fresh headers mapping per request and never mutate client-level objects. i'll put up a PR.
jean: long-term: add typed middleware hook signatures, an immutable Headers type (Mapping[str,str]), and an examples/observability/py app that demonstrates structlog+otel+async client working under concurrency with tests.
sam: please include a small unit test that reproduces the race and a microbenchmark for the per-request-copy cost. we need to document the perf tradeoff.
ci-bot: created issues #4230 and #4231 and linked to the PR template.
maria: assign tasks: derek -> bugfix PR (async headers immutability), jean -> typed hooks + example sample + structlog helper, sam -> reproducible test and microbench. i'll review. :thumbsup:
